Create a slice AST node

Source: R/ast.R
ast_slice.Rd

One node type covers the whole slice family (slice()/slice_head()/ slice_tail()/slice_min()/slice_max()), distinguished by mode – unlike most other verbs (which each get their own ast_* constructor), these five share the same "select a subset of rows, in some order, from a single input" shape and (mostly) the same n=/prop= sizing rule, so one node with a mode-specific field set avoids several near-identical constructors/lowering functions/optimizer barrier entries. slice_sample() and every grouped variant are out of scope for this node (Phase 3 scope decision, see R/slice.R) and keep using the CPU fallback (R/fallback.R) instead.

Usage

ast_slice(
  input,
  mode,
  amount = NULL,
  is_prop = NULL,
  raw_indices = NULL,
  order_col = NULL,
  order_is_temp = FALSE,
  descending = NULL,
  with_ties = NULL,
  na_rm = NULL,
  bracket_arg = NULL,
  bracket_call = NULL,
  rows_resolved = FALSE,
  top_k = FALSE,
  group_cols = NULL,
  by_first = FALSE
)

Arguments

input

Input AST node

mode

One of "head", "tail", "index", "rank", "rank_grouped", "bracket" (tibble x[i, ] row subscript in raw_indices, NA / out-of-range give NA rows)

amount

For mode "head"/"tail"/"rank": the raw (unresolved) n/prop value (sign preserved; resolved against the actual row count only at lowering time, see src/ops_common.hpp::compute_slice_size())

is_prop

For mode "head"/"tail"/"rank": TRUE if amount is a prop, FALSE if it's an n

raw_indices

For mode "index": the unresolved numeric index vector from slice()'s dots (may contain 0/NA/duplicates/out-of-range/ negative values – fully resolved only at lowering time, since negative indices and out-of-range dropping both need the actual row count)

order_col

For mode "rank": the column name (in input's output schema) to rank by – always a real column name, even when order_by was a computed expression (see order_is_temp)

order_is_temp

For mode "rank": TRUE if order_col is a synthetic column added by a wrapping ast_mutate (computed order_by, e.g. slice_min(df, x + y)) that must NOT appear in the final output – mirrors distinct()'s same computed-key pattern (R/distinct.R)

descending

For mode "rank": FALSE for slice_min(), TRUE for slice_max()

with_ties, na_rm

For mode "rank": as documented on slice_min()/slice_max()

bracket_arg, bracket_call, rows_resolved

For mode "bracket": raw_indices is either already resolved to 1-based positions against the real row count (rows_resolved = TRUE, NA = all-NA row), or still the user's raw subscript, in which case bracket_arg (the user's subscript expression) and bracket_call (the [ call) label any error raised when it is resolved at lowering

top_k

For mode "rank": TRUE on a node the optimizer made from arrange(x) |> head(n) (rewrite_slice_over_arrange()); the node is then slice_min(x, n, with_ties = FALSE) and nothing else

group_cols, by_first

For mode == "rank_grouped" (F115, a grouped slice_min()/slice_max() on a numeric or date key, run by gpu_slice_rank_grouped()): the grouping columns, and whether the groups come out in order of their first row (by=/.by=) rather than sorted by key (group_by()). The other rank fields mean what they do for "rank".

Value

An ast_slice node
